title: Agent-Friendly Repository Architecture: Deeper Research Finding

tldr.content: A repository becomes agent-friendly when its context is scoped, its boundaries and contracts are explicit, its permissions are host-enforced, and its changes are validated through deterministic tests, trace evaluation, and human review. The strongest new conclusion is that optimization must be empirical: task datasets, trajectories, grader calibration, safety tests, and reproducible environments are required before autonomy or parallelism is widened.

executiveSummary.content:
This DEEP hybrid investigation combined five independent tracks: cross-agent instruction behavior, architecture and contracts, agent evaluation, security controls, and current repository evidence.

```text
context -> boundaries/contracts -> sandbox/policy -> change validation
      -> trace + outcome evaluation -> calibrated review -> controlled autonomy
```

The research rejects two simplistic strategies: a large root prompt is not an architecture, and passing repository tests is not sufficient evidence of agent quality. Current vendor documentation shows materially different instruction loading and precedence semantics. Standards support explicit contracts, compatibility, ownership, and telemetry. Security sources consistently place enforcement outside model instructions. Evaluation sources require task-grounded outcomes, trajectory evidence, calibrated graders, pinned environments, and human review. Agent-specific productivity improvement remains unverified.

keyFindings.content:
K1 [partially-supported] Use concise layered context, but treat filename, discovery, precedence, and size behavior as runtime-specific rather than portable assumptions. [ref-openai-agents][ref-anthropic-memory][ref-github-instructions][ref-gemini-context]

K2 [supported] Define coherent capabilities with explicit public contracts, compatibility rules, ownership, and stable physical discoverability; do not optimize by making every unit arbitrarily small. [ref-microsoft-microservices][ref-openapi][ref-json-schema][ref-google-compat]

K3 [supported] Treat instructions and tool metadata as guidance, never authorization; enforce side-effect policy with sandboxing, least privilege, network controls, approvals, validation, and auditability. [ref-openai-security][ref-mcp-tools][ref-mcp-security][ref-nist-ssdf]

K4 [supported] Evaluate final artifacts and agent trajectories separately, using task-grounded deterministic checks plus rubric-based behavior evaluation. [ref-google-evaluate][ref-openai-trace][ref-swebench]

K5 [supported] Calibrate automated graders against expert judgments, retain per-task evidence, classify infrastructure failures separately, and pin the evaluation environment and run identity. [ref-openai-graders][ref-swebench][ref-nist-measure]

K6 [partially-supported] Durable journals, correlated telemetry, and artifact identity are necessary foundations for inspectability and recovery, but their outcome benefit depends on actual producer/consumer enforcement. [ref-w3c-trace][ref-otel-scope][ref-nist-measure]

K7 [unverifiable] These practices improve coding-agent productivity, autonomy, or cost. No retrieved source provides causal comparative evidence. [ref-nist-measure]

detailSections.content:
### Context portability
Codex documents root-to-working-directory discovery, nearest-file precedence, fallback filenames, and a 32 KiB aggregate default. Claude Code documents managed, user, project, local, and lazy nested loading, but reads CLAUDE.md rather than AGENTS.md natively and recommends under 200 lines. GitHub Copilot has feature-dependent repository, path, organization, personal, and AGENTS.md behavior. Gemini CLI concatenates configured context files and does not clearly document universal nearest-wins semantics or a fixed limit. Therefore use AGENTS.md as a useful common layer, add thin adapters where necessary, and test each supported runtime. [ref-openai-agents][ref-anthropic-memory][ref-github-instructions][ref-gemini-context]

### Architecture boundaries
Model boundaries around coherent capabilities and change coupling. OpenAPI makes HTTP capabilities understandable without source access; JSON Schema defines validation and documentation vocabularies; Google API guidance separates source, wire, and semantic compatibility and prohibits unsafe additive changes. Stable directory and package names also affect generated consumers. Keep state and schemas owned, dependencies directional, and compatibility policy explicit. [ref-microsoft-microservices][ref-openapi][ref-json-schema][ref-google-compat][ref-google-layout]

### Safety architecture
Sandboxing and approvals are separate controls. Default to workspace-scoped access, disabled or proxied egress, isolated credentials, explicit approval for sensitive reads and writes, and boundary validation. Treat repository issues, web pages, READMEs, tool descriptions, hooks, plugins, and MCP servers as untrusted content. MCP additionally requires origin validation, secure authorization, audience-bound tokens, PKCE, and SSRF defenses. Hooks are useful but not complete enforcement boundaries. [ref-openai-security][ref-openai-internet][ref-mcp-tools][ref-mcp-security][ref-mcp-auth][ref-github-hooks]

### Evaluation architecture
Use a versioned task dataset containing repository revision, request, allowed tools, environment, expected artifact, acceptance tests, and run metadata. Apply deterministic tests in a pinned sandbox, capture tool and edit trajectories, grade final artifacts separately, retain raw per-instance evidence, and distinguish agent, test, patch, environment, timeout, and evaluator failures. Use exact trajectory matching only for mandatory ordering constraints; use calibrated rubrics for valid alternative strategies. [ref-google-evaluate][ref-openai-trace][ref-openai-graders][ref-swebench][ref-nist-measure]

### Operational feedback
Telemetry should join run identity, parent span, repository/skill digest, model/runtime, tool, permission decision, state transition, status, duration, and redacted error class. OpenTelemetry instrumentation scope and W3C Trace Context provide attribution and propagation mechanisms. Retain enough evidence to diagnose failures, but never make secrets or raw sensitive prompts the default telemetry payload. [ref-otel-scope][ref-otel-trace][ref-w3c-trace]

### Current-repository implications
The local repository evidence reviewed during this run shows strong foundations: explicit human-mediated skill boundaries, immutable artifact identity, JSON schema registries, resolver and projection separation, lifecycle journals, and deterministic CI migration work. The same evidence leaves decision-blocking questions: whether all runtime paths enforce contracts and lifecycle transitions, whether local-source citations fit the canonical JSON schema, whether compatibility matrices cover all producers/consumers, whether stale artifact indexes indicate synchronization defects, and whether live agent behavior has been measured. These are workspace-local observations recorded as research context, not externally citable claims.

recommendation.content:
Adopt a layered, evidence-gated repository architecture.

1. Context: publish concise root guidance plus narrowly scoped subsystem guidance; maintain runtime adapters and test discovery/precedence on every supported agent. [ref-openai-agents][ref-anthropic-memory][ref-github-instructions][ref-gemini-context]
2. Boundaries: define capability ownership, typed input/output/error contracts, compatibility dimensions, stable paths, and dependency direction. [ref-openapi][ref-json-schema][ref-google-compat][ref-google-layout]
3. Safety: run tools in an isolated, least-privilege environment; default network off; isolate secrets; require approval for sensitive actions; enforce policy at tool/host boundaries; test prompt injection, SSRF, exfiltration, hook tampering, and approval bypass. [ref-openai-security][ref-openai-internet][ref-mcp-security][ref-nist-ssdf]
4. Validation: require deterministic format, lint, type, unit, contract, integration, security, protected-file, and diff checks appropriate to the repository, with CI and human review gates. [ref-github-actions][ref-github-branches][ref-anthropic-agents]
5. Evaluation: maintain a pinned task dataset and environment; capture trajectories and final artifacts; use component graders calibrated against experts; set per-metric safety and quality thresholds; retain evidence and report infrastructure failures separately. [ref-google-evaluate][ref-openai-graders][ref-swebench][ref-nist-measure]
6. Autonomy: widen permissions or parallelism only when repeated repository-local evaluation shows improved outcomes without safety, recovery, or review regressions. This is a recommendation and validation hypothesis, not a proven causal result.

unverifiedClaims.content:
Decision-blocking: no universal cross-agent instruction precedence, size limit, or AGENTS.md conformance behavior was established.

Decision-blocking: no live agent evaluation was run for this repository, so activation, trajectory, recovery, and task-success rates are unknown.

Material risk: vendor security documentation describes controls and limitations but does not independently establish exploit resistance.

Material risk: benchmark scores are task- and harness-specific and do not establish general engineering competence.

Material risk: LLM graders can be hacked or disagree with experts; calibration and human sampling are required.

Context-dependent: microservice guidance does not require splitting a monorepo; apply the boundary principles without importing unnecessary operational complexity.

Context-dependent: OpenAI Evals/Graders lifecycle and current APIs require verification before implementation; this finding intentionally recommends evaluation practices, not a vendor API choice.

Informational: local repository strengths and gaps were inspected read-only and may change with concurrent worktree changes.

processAppendix.content:
Triage: DEEP, hybrid. Assumption: the question concerns both general agentic-development architecture and the current skills repository.

Tracks: (1) instruction portability; (2) architecture boundaries/contracts; (3) evaluation and reproducibility; (4) security and tool controls; (5) local post-migration architecture. Five independent read-only researchers returned structured evidence. No API key, secret, browser session, code execution, or persistent scratch evidence was used.

Challenge: an independent challenger should test whether the conclusion overclaims portability, causal benefit, enforcement, or benchmark validity. The synthesized finding preemptively narrows those claims and records them as partially-supported or unverifiable where sources establish mechanisms but not outcomes.

Judge status: the prior artifact’s judge found completeness and citation defects; this JSON run changes the canonical format and expands the evidence set. A final independent file-level judge could not be completed because workspace isolation removed the prior run artifact during adjudication. This is a residual limitation, not a claimed pass.

DEEP verification: claims are atomic and assigned verdicts; reference IDs are defined; the projection order is fixed; no declared artifacts exist; credentials and personal data are excluded. The protected baseline was already dirty at intake and changed concurrently, so this run cannot attribute unrelated worktree changes to the research.
